paper.title_en: Little Red Dots from Primordial Vacuum Bubbles
paper.abstract_en: Quantum tunneling transverse to the inflaton trajectory can produce $10^6$--$10^8M_\odot$ primordial black holes at the abundance of JWST's little red dots, without the enhanced curvature perturbations excluded by limits on CMB spectral distortions. Rare vacuum bubbles nucleate during a brief interval of inflation and later form black holes, with adjustable mass and abundance and a narrow mass spectrum of percent-level width. The leading constraint, from accretion, is satisfied for a population matching the bright little red dots even if all the emitted radiation escapes as hard X-rays.
